clue.text: Have nothing to do with free ticket winning

blocks.note: a pass is a ticket that lets you in without paying
a team that is up is ahead, winning

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to touch a free ticket even though it is a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something up is to decline an offer or opportunity, refusing any involvement with it.

clue.text: Story-teller having to sit up after first of allegories

indicators.note: first of tells us to keep only the opening letter of the following word
in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
after places the reversed sitting word behind the single letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of allegories
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A fabulist must sit up straight after beginning a collection of allegories.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author credited with the famous fables, so he is the archetypal teller of moral tales.

clue.text: Decoy's snout

blocks.note: first meaning: a bird tied to a stool to lure others, hence a lure
second meaning: British slang for a police informer

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the nose of a decoy animal; snout is also British underworld slang for an informer, someone who grasses to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The term originally meant a pigeon used to lure wild birds, and later came to mean a police informer or spy.

clue.text: Peg describing a row about bishop in cocktail lounge?

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the peg goes around the next letter
about means surrounding, so the row word wraps around the bishop

blocks.note: a peg is a pin used to fasten things
taken as written
to row is to oar a boat
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone pegs a row of drinkers arguing over a bishop in a smart bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel; here it is the verb for rowing a boat. Each half is its own container.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano bar is a lounge where cocktails are served to live piano music; the question mark admits the definition is loose.

clue.text: Very bad period of time for a rural community

blocks.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
ill means bad, as in ill effects
an age is a long period

explanation.surface: A countryside settlement goes through a terrible spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A village is a small settlement in the countryside, a community of country dwellers.

clue.text: Large container porter brought in for a man

indicators.note: brought in for means put in place of, so the beer replaces the single letter named next

blocks.note: a vat is a big tank or tub
porter is a dark beer, so ale stands in for it
the letter that is swapped out

explanation.surface: A railway porter brings in a large trunk for a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a luggage carrier; it is the dark beer, which takes the place of the A in the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's personal servant is traditionally called his man, which is exactly what a valet is.

clue.text: I suffer over lad's affair

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the preceding pair of words is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to ail is to be ill, to suffer
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to suffering over a young man's romantic entanglement.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both I and the suffering word together, so the I ends up after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship, an illicit affair.

clue.text: Suitable whip

blocks.note: first meaning: fitting, proper (adjective)
second meaning: to steal or take for oneself (verb)

explanation.walkthrough: Whip looks like a lash; it is the slang verb for pinching something.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means fitting; as a verb it means to take something for your own use, which is what whipping it means.

clue.text: Select rice, ultimately — low in calories

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the final letter of rice
lite is the marketing spelling for low-calorie food

explanation.surface: A diet tip: choose rice, since in the end it is low in calories.
explanation.walkthrough: Select looks like a verb instructing you; it is the adjective for a choice group.
explanation.definitionFit: A select group is an exclusive, chosen few, which is the meaning of an elite.

clue.text: Recognise celebrities? Do this, perhaps, if struck

blocks.note: first meaning: literally spotting famous people
second meaning: the dazzled vision after a blow on the head

explanation.walkthrough: Struck could mean starstruck; it is a knock on the head that makes you see stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting famous people is literally seeing stars, and a hard blow to the head makes a person see flashing lights, idiomatically seeing stars.

clue.text: Little tip for final applicants

blocks.note: short means little in height or length
to list is to tip or lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A small piece of advice for the last few job candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip suggests advice or a gratuity; it is the verb for leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the reduced set of candidates left in contention for a post after the first sift.

clue.text: Distinctive character in Newmarket hostelry

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words as written

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A pub in Newmarket, the racing town, has its own special atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values of a community or institution.

clue.text: Film male, one fielding after start of test

indicators.note: start of keeps just the opening letter of the next word
after puts the male and the fielder behind the single letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of test
he is the male pronoun
third man is a cricket fielding position behind the slips

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a man fielding at the start of a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, and third man is a fielding position on the off side behind the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Third Man is the 1949 Carol Reed movie starring Orson Welles, set in postwar Vienna.

clue.text: Without opener, field a substitute

indicators.note: without its opener means the first letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: a preserve is an area of land kept for game, a field of activity

explanation.surface: A cricket team without its opening batsman has to field a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: Field reads as the verb of putting out a team; it is the noun for an area or domain.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve is a player kept back to come on in place of another, a substitute.

clue.text: Run off in polished stilettos after parade?

annotation.answer: SHOW A CLEAN PAIR OF HEELS

indicators.note: after puts the polished footwear behind the parading word

blocks.note: to parade something is to show it off
stilettos are high heels, and polished ones are clean

explanation.surface: A model runs away down the catwalk in shiny high heels after the fashion show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads parade as a noun; it is the verb to display.
explanation.definitionFit: To show a clean pair of heels is an idiom meaning to run away fast, leaving pursuers behind.

clue.text: Explain Pinter's opening in Betrayal

indicators.note: opening keeps only the first letter of the playwright's name
in places that letter inside the word for betrayal

blocks.note: the first letter of Pinter
a sellout is an act of betrayal

explanation.surface: A critic explains how Harold Pinter's play Betrayal opens.
explanation.walkthrough: Betrayal is a real Pinter play, which disguises its role as a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell something out is to explain it in plain, detailed terms.

clue.text: Urgently heading for teleprinter after distress call one received

indicators.note: heading for picks out the first letter of the next word
received means taken in, so the call holds the number
after places the letter at the end of the rest

blocks.note: SOS is the international distress signal
taken as written
the first letter of teleprinter

explanation.surface: An emergency message comes through on a teleprinter and someone rushes to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soonest, as in at the earliest possible moment, means with the greatest urgency.

clue.text: Class take this after dope

indicators.note: after places the handing-over word behind the information word

blocks.note: SP, short for starting price, is British slang for the inside information
here! is what you say when handing someone something

explanation.surface: A teacher tells a class to take something after hearing about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope looks like drugs; it is information, and the SP is a British phrase for the full facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere can mean a social class or rank, as in moving in a different sphere of society.

clue.text: Hope to have most of jelly with helping

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the jelly word is dropped

blocks.note: aspic is a savoury meat jelly
a ration is an allotted portion, a helping

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for most of the jelly with a second helping.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a hope or ambition, something one longs to achieve.

clue.text: Figure alien must be breaking law

indicators.note: breaking into something means sitting inside it, so the alien goes into the law

blocks.note: ET is the film alien, a crossword staple
a statute is a written law

explanation.surface: A sum shows that an illegal immigrant must be breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure looks like a number in a calculation; it is a small sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A statuette is a small statue, a carved or moulded figure.

clue.text: Lunacy omitting son in senseless action

indicators.note: omitting means leaving the named letter out

blocks.note: lunacy is madness
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Dropping a son from the team is called madness, a senseless act.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanity is silliness or pointlessness, so a senseless deed is an inanity.

clue.text: Timid type, a bishop settling in London, maybe, in an overcrowded area

indicators.note: settling in means coming to rest inside, so these letters go within the city word

blocks.note: a rabbit is a timid creature, or a feeble person
Cobbett called London the Great Wen, a wen being a swelling
taken as written
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A shy bishop moves to London and finds himself in a crowded district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Wen was William Cobbett's scornful name for London, so a wen is a crossword name for a sprawling city.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit warren is a maze of burrows, and figuratively any cramped, densely packed building or district.

clue.text: Invoice committee for hoarding

blocks.note: a bill is an invoice
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A committee is sent an invoice for stockpiling goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoarding suggests stockpiling; in British English it is also a large outdoor advertising board.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarding is the British term for a large outdoor panel for posters, which Americans call a billboard.

clue.text: Turn on wench providing winch

blocks.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle
a wench is an old word for a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A sailor turns to a girl for a lifting device.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a hoisting machine with a horizontal drum turned by a crank, a kind of winch.

clue.text: Food pleasing to the eye, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard rather than seen, so the word is spoken

blocks.note: fair means good-looking

explanation.surface: Someone claims a dish looks attractive on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is the food and drink provided at a meal, as in simple country fare.

clue.text: With book in college defining game

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the college word

blocks.note: and means with, in addition
B is the abbreviation for book
a hall is a residential college or the college itself

explanation.surface: A book at a university college defines a particular sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Handball is a team sport in which players throw a ball into a goal, so it is a game.

clue.text: So ended a broadcast about married heroine in play

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the married abbreviation

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A radio play concludes with the married heroine's fate broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is the wife of Othello in Shakespeare's tragedy, killed by her jealous husband.

clue.text: Guys in principle responsible for a block of flats

indicators.note: in places the guys inside the principle word

blocks.note: guys are men
a tenet is a principle or belief

explanation.surface: Men of principle are put in charge of an apartment building.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into separate rented flats, often run-down.

clue.text: Fruit drink that's delicious in the East

blocks.note: nectar is the drink of the gods, anything delicious to drink
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A delicious fruit drink is found in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Tiresome nanny and I go out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child complains that the nanny is wearisome, so they will both go out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annoying irritates or wearies you, which is what tiresome means.

clue.text: Problem with arson, a crucial matter?

blocks.note: first meaning, humorous: the question of setting fires
second meaning: a pressing topic of the day

explanation.walkthrough: The first part takes the phrase literally, as an issue about burning; the question mark marks the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An urgent topic that everyone is debating is idiomatically called a burning question or issue.

clue.text: Nerve and audacity shown in hold-up

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for courage
neck means cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: A robber shows nerve and daring in a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: Hold-up suggests a robbery; it is a delay. Bottle and neck are both British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottleneck is a narrow point that slows traffic or progress, causing a delay or hold-up.

clue.text: Substantial bidding

blocks.note: first meaning: significant, effective
second meaning: ordering someone, as in doing someone's bidding

explanation.walkthrough: Bidding suggests an auction; it is instructing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling argument is a weighty, significant one, and telling someone to do something is bidding them.

clue.text: Group after sound system for convention

indicators.note: after places the group word behind the sound system

blocks.note: a stereo is a hi-fi
a type is a class or group

explanation.surface: A band follows a sound check ahead of a big gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Convention suggests a conference; it is a fixed, conventional idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a fixed, standard image of a person or thing, a received convention.

clue.text: Enthusiastic card game in plant

blocks.note: red-hot means passionate, fervent
poker is the betting card game

explanation.surface: A keen gambler is caught up in a rigged card game.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like a set-up or stooge; it is a flowering garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-hot poker, or kniphofia, is a garden perennial with spikes of red and yellow flowers.

clue.text: Possible result of game being in grass allowed to roam wild

indicators.note: roaming wild means wandering without order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cattle are allowed to roam freely on the grass of a football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A football match ending nil-nil is a goalless draw, one possible outcome of a game.

clue.text: Inexperienced in a good way, that is belonging to an upper-class set?

blocks.note: green means new to something, naive
well means in a good manner
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A novice, it seems, is doing nicely in posh society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Green Wellie brigade is a British label for upper-class country types who wear green rubber boots, wellies being wellington boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Green-wellie describes the British county set, the well-off rural gentry known for their Hunter boots.

clue.text: Sensible paraglider heading this way eventually?

blocks.note: first meaning: practical and realistic
second meaning, literal: where a gliding flyer ends up

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the idiom literally: a paraglider eventually comes down to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A down-to-earth person is practical, realistic and unpretentious, which is to say sensible.

clue.text: Insensitive column, a problem for the editor?

blocks.note: dead means numb, without feeling
a line is a row or file, a column

explanation.surface: A tactless newspaper column causes trouble for its editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Column suggests a newspaper piece; it is a line, as of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the time limit for submitting copy, a constant worry for anyone editing a paper.

clue.text: Outgoing person, former scout, entering IOM races

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the scout goes inside the race abbreviation

blocks.note: ex means former
the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle racing on the Isle of Man
a Rover was a senior Scout

explanation.surface: A sociable ex-Scout signs up for the Isle of Man motorbike races.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, home of the TT motorcycle races; Rover Scouts were the older section of the Scout movement.

clue.text: Tire oneself out on visit by Italian

blocks.note: on and over both mean concerning, as in a row over money
to do a place is to visit it as a tourist
It is the abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A tourist on a trip with an Italian guide wears themselves out.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo it is to work too hard or exert oneself excessively, wearing oneself out.

clue.text: Dam — spooky no end

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the preceding word is cut

blocks.note: weird means eerie

explanation.surface: A spooky reservoir, and the exclamation 'Damn, spooky no end!'
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam built across a river to control its flow.

clue.text: Under pressure, made and delivered a sermon

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the following word beneath the pressure letter

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
to make a place is to reach it

explanation.surface: A vicar under pressure wrote and gave a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to deliver a sermon, so the past tense means a sermon was given.

clue.text: Long distance traveller, finished with school

blocks.note: through means done, finished
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A traveller who has finished school heads off on a long journey.
explanation.walkthrough: School looks like a noun; it is the verb to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: A through train runs the whole route without changes, travelling long distances non-stop.

clue.text: Type of car difficult to beat

blocks.note: hard means difficult
to top something is to beat it

explanation.surface: A model of car that is hard to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid roof, often removable, as opposed to a soft-top convertible.

clue.text: TV game show runs into considerable trouble

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the runs letter sits within the trouble word

blocks.note: big means large, considerable
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
bother means trouble

explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is the reality television show in which housemates are filmed and voted out, a competition format.

clue.text: Sleep so long on top of sofabed

indicators.note: top of, in a down clue, keeps the first letter of the next word
on in a down clue places the farewell above the single letter

blocks.note: so long and bye-bye are both farewells
the first letter of sofabed

clue.text: Stand as excursion party returned

explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand, as for a camera.

clue.text: Drop daughter with it by church

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.definitionFit: Ditch is informal for discarding or abandoning something, letting it fall from your plans.

clue.text: Disgusting old boy linked with ugly incident

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to make a scene is to cause an ugly public row

explanation.surface: A former pupil is implicated in a nasty public row, which is disgraceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive or repugnant, utterly disgusting.

clue.text: Pronounce fit

blocks.note: first meaning: to voice a letter or word (verb)
second meaning: healthy, in good condition (adjective)

explanation.walkthrough: Pronounce fit reads like a doctor's verdict, but the two words are separate meanings.

clue.text: Non-professionals playing are a must

indicators.note: playing suggests the words are being played about with and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Unpaid players are essential to the team.

clue.text: Detest rough bar small house installed

clue.text: One putting clothes on sideboard

blocks.note: first meaning: a theatre assistant who dresses an actor
second meaning: a kitchen cupboard with shelves

clue.text: Plant in trouble had backing

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble
taken as written
